name: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
problem: Fitting a new task from a handful of examples required fine-tuning on thousands of times more task data.
mechanism: Interleaves vision and text in one sequence and inserts PERCEIVER RESAMPLER blocks between the frozen vision backbone and the frozen language model. The resampler maps a variable-length visual token sequence to a small fixed number of vectors via learned latent queries with cross-attention, so the LM's sequence length grows by a constant regardless of image count or video length.
notes:
NeurIPS 2022 (arXiv comment 'In Proceedings of Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)'; the NeurIPS 2022 proceedings index contains the title). Weights were never released, hence research-only and open_weights false. THE KEY INFERENCE MECHANISM FOR THIS REPO IS THE PERCEIVER RESAMPLER: it makes vision-token count a tunable constant independent of input resolution and modality count. Every later resampler-based VLM (Q-Former in BLIP-2, SALMONN's audio resampler) is a variation on this, and it is the direct alternative to pruning, with the tradeoff that resampling is lossy but fixed-cost while pruning keeps full fidelity only where it matters.
